# Phase Two — Improved Brainstorm After Gevurah

The Awtsmoos conceals and reveals, so a boundless dream can enter form;
Awtsmoos.com needs a movie covenant small enough to test, yet wide enough to survive the storm.

## Revised center of gravity
The project should not attempt to “merge four apps.” It should establish three shared contracts and make each app choose how much of them it consumes:

1. **Movie Contract** — declarative document, validation, time, capabilities, feature inventory.
2. **Asset Intent Contract** — movie nodes request existing procedural generators through stable descriptors.
3. **UI Recipe Contract** — declarative mobile-first studio shell and reusable app UI pieces.

Everything else is adapter territory.

## Movie contract minimum viable completeness
The first implementation should support enough vocabulary to build the required proof movie without pretending to cover infinite cinema on day one:
- movie metadata and exact duration;
- scenes with explicit duration/order;
- layers with start/end windows;
- transforms and opacity;
- reusable assets/actors;
- 2D shapes and text;
- chart/tutorial primitives;
- 3D primitive/procedural asset references;
- particles;
- camera cues;
- keyframes and easing;
- transitions;
- captions/audio cue metadata;
- groups;
- validation and feature inventory.

Extensibility comes from a typed node registry/capability catalog instead of adding speculative dozens of fields.

## Runtime model
The compiler should create a small immutable-ish execution artifact:
- normalized document;
- ordered scene spans;
- asset lookup map;
- actor lookup map;
- capability requirements;
- warnings/errors;
- total duration;
- helper for `frameAt(time)` or `resolve(time)`.

A resolved frame need not contain raster pixels. It contains the semantic scene state at time `t`, including active layers and interpolated values. Render adapters turn that state into pixels.

## 2D realization strategy
Prefer Canvas 2D for the first shared renderer because it is browser-native and ideal for text, shapes, diagrams, charts, callouts, and particles. Keep a renderer registry so SVG/DOM can be added later.

The Canvas adapter can remain generic if it only knows canonical layer types and simple drawing operations. Procedural character/complex image layers can supply a bitmap/canvas source through asset adapters.

## 3D realization strategy
Do not write a new Three.js engine. Build a thin adapter that can map canonical movie cues into whichever shared Three/procedural runtime is already public. Where existing core provides asset generators but not a full browser Three scene host, the flagship can bind an app/runtime adapter rather than infecting core contracts with global `THREE` assumptions.

## Character strategy
Canonical actors are identity records. A scene layer refers to `actorId` and animation/action cues. The adapter resolves the actor through existing procedural human/rig systems. This allows one character identity to recur across scenes and camera angles.

## Infographic/tutorial strategy
Create first-class semantic primitives rather than making AI hand-author hundreds of low-level rectangles:
- `callout`
- `arrow`
- `chart`
- `progress`
- `stepCard`
- `highlightBox`
- `codePanel`
- `comparison`

Adapters may expand these into shapes/text. This keeps AI output compact and repairable.

## Particle strategy
Canonical particle layers should accept named presets plus deterministic seed and a bounded property bag. The adapter can map to the existing procedural particle engine when compatible or use a simple Canvas fallback for 2D-only apps.

## UI strategy
The shared UI grammar should focus on reducing studio boilerplate, not replacing every component system. Initial node types:
- element
- text
- button/action
- list/repeater
- input/field
- conditional
- slot/custom mount

Studio helpers then describe higher-level composition:
- toolbar
- preview surface
- navigator tabs
- sheet/panel
- timeline container
- inspector container
- status/export area

This hierarchy keeps the low-level renderer generic while studio recipes remain expressive.

## Security and AI safety
- whitelist tags/attributes;
- no inline scripts;
- no raw event source strings;
- action names resolve through registry;
- text is text by default;
- URL policies for media sources;
- movie nodes validated before adapters receive them;
- capability discovery lets AI choose valid alternatives.

## Integration strategy by app
- **Animator:** expose canonical import/export and use its strong character/camera/procedural systems as adapters. Avoid rewriting deep animator internals unless a parallel agent already provides a stable bridge.
- **Nesher Studio:** expose canonical project/movie conversion and export provider. Reuse NLE/export rather than moving it wholesale into core.
- **Video Editor:** support canonical simple clips/scenes/captions and preserve compact timeline UX.
- **Mitzvah Studio:** support canonical visual-object conversion and shared UI recipes where easy, preserving inspector/outliner workflow.
- **Awtsmoos Studio:** consume all shared contracts directly and become the integration proof.

## Proof movie design
Twelve scenes at fifteen seconds each is structurally simple and exactly 180 seconds. Not every scene must have the same pacing internally; each can contain multiple beats/keyframes.

Possible scene arc:
1. Creation burst — particles + title + cosmic 3D reveal.
2. World emergence — procedural terrain/city, crane/wide camera.
3. Character arrival — two reusable people, medium/low-angle shots.
4. Tutorial board — 2D steps, arrows, kinetic labels.
5. Data story — animated bars/line/progress and callouts.
6. Split dimensions — 2D overlays over 3D object/environment.
7. Dialogue/performance — close-up/over-shoulder character shots.
8. Procedural build — architecture/shape assembly with annotations.
9. Motion lesson — paths, easing comparison, particles/trails.
10. Climax — orbit camera, particle field, layered text, environment motion.
11. Recap — cards, chart summary, character callback.
12. Credits/revelation — calm camera, typography, particles, fade.

## Verification strategy refined
Unit tests prove pure contracts. Browser tests prove adapters/UI. The proof movie doubles as an integration fixture. Export is validated by artifact existence, non-zero size, duration metadata if inspectable, and representative visual frames where practical.

Phase Two conclusion: one pure semantic core, thin render/export adapters, narrow secure UI grammar, and a flagship app that proves the whole chain end-to-end.
